subject: Post-call exec recap: SolsticeHealth — next steps and risks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara@solsticehealth.com>, Tom Rivera <tom@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call exec recap: SolsticeHealth — next steps and risks

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciated the open conversation. Below is a concise exec-friendly recap and suggested next steps so your CFO/exec sponsor and procurement have a clear path forward.

TL;DR
- Problem: Fragmented clinical notes ingestion + long (20–30s) summarization latency causing clinician friction and missed SLAs.
- Goal: Reduce summarization latency to sub-3s 95th percentile, integrate into Epic workflow, and drive 20% clinician time-savings within Q3.
- Ask: Exec sponsor confirmation (CFO Daniel Park), procurement path + PO timing, security questionnaire review.

Key pain points discussed
- Current pipeline: batch-ingest nightly; near-real-time cases blow past SLAs during peak.
- Cost sensitivity: strict quarterly budget windows — procurement only approves within existing FY quarter.
- Security: SOC 2 + regional data controls required for PHI-handling workflows.

Business outcomes (what Solstice would measure)
- 95th pct latency < 3s for summary endpoint on target patient segments
- 20% reduction in clinician documentation time in pilot group
- Predictable cost per 1k summaries (target: <$0.50/summary)

Risks and mitigations
- Data residency: you require regional controls — Redwood Private or dedicated pools can be scoped (we flagged this to our infra team).
- Procurement timing: your FY window constraint — recommend aligning contract signature by end of May to fit Q3 deployment.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Marissa -> Send mutual action plan (MAP) + first-pass SOW and SOC2 evidence (today EOD) [attachment: SLH_Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf]
2) Solstice -> Confirm exec sponsor (name + best time) and procurement contact (by Tue 2027-04-06)
3) Schedule procurement + legal intro call (30m) to review standard terms and PO path (Marissa to propose times)
4) Tech sync: Scoped POC success criteria and data flow (Marcus to join) — target wk of 4/19

Attachments: SLH_Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf (mutual action plan), SOC2-evidence.zip (sample evidence index)

If this aligns, I’ll send the MAP/SOW and propose 2 time slots for the procurement call.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0148

--

Date: 2027-04-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call exec recap: SolsticeHealth — next steps and risks

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Helpful.

Confirming a few items from our side:
- Exec sponsor: Daniel Park (CFO) — he asked to see the MAP and a 1‑page summary of risk controls before committing to a procurement call.
- Procurement contact: procurement@solsticehealth.com (I’ll loop them in once we have the MAP).
- Timeline: We’re targeting a Q3 pilot but need contract signed by end of May to secure FY budget.

I’ll review the MAP today and aim to get procurement on a quick sync early next week. Also, can you include a short note on rollback/fallthrough behavior and whether Redwood supports automatic failover to a cheaper model variant? That’s a question Daniel will ask.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Klein
VP Product, Solstice Health
sara@solsticehealth.com

Subject: Internal: SolsticeHealth — exec recap + recommend credit package

Marissa / Marcus — quick internal note.

Good recap to the prospect. A couple of points from the leadership / deal desk perspective:
- Exec ask: Daniel will want hard SLAs on latency and a clear procurement path — work with Marcus on the technical appendix for the MAP.
- Credit ask: Given the pilot and the procurement timing risk, recommend offering a 2-month credit on usage for the pilot (structured as prepaid credit tied to deployment milestones). This helps overcome Daniel’s cost sensitivity and accelerates procurement.
- Approvals: If Solstice pushes PO timing beyond May, we should consider a 30-day procurement escalation with Sales Ops.

If you want, I can join procurement call — would be useful to position SLA flexibility and sign-off criteria.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
